text:
Done.

The one guarantee is now three, stated separately in the AtomicFiles scaladoc because they have different implementations, different tests, and different platform support:

1. ATOMIC VISIBILITY — a reader sees no file or the complete file, never a partial one. rename(2). Unconditional.
2. SINGLE PUBLISHER / NO REPLACE — at most one writer succeeds per destination. The sidecar lock, now on every path after C1. Cited to AtomicCrossProcessSuite, which observed two and three simultaneous "winners" before the lock was applied — so this claim rests on measurement, not assertion.
3. CRASH DURABILITY — best effort, and explicitly labelled so.

The durability gap was real and is now partly closed. stageAndMove forced the file CONTENTS, which makes the bytes durable, and never forced the containing directory, which is what makes the RENAME durable — so a crash could lose a published file whose contents were already on stable storage while the class doc claimed "forces its contents to stable storage". A new forceDirectory is called after every successful move.

It cannot be a guarantee, and the doc says so rather than implying otherwise. Opening a directory as a channel is not portable: Linux permits it, macOS rejects it with IsADirectory. forceDirectory therefore RETURNS whether the platform allowed it instead of swallowing the failure, so a consumer that genuinely needs crash durability can discover it was not achieved. On this development machine (macOS/APFS) it returns false; on Linux it closes the gap.

Filesystem qualification added and deliberately narrow: verified on local POSIX filesystems (APFS, ext4); NOT verified on NFS or Lustre, because advisory FileLock semantics over NFS depend on server and mount options and cross-client rename atomicity is weaker than local rename(2). A consumer needing guarantee 2 or 3 on a network filesystem must establish it for that deployment.

Deliberately NOT done, agreeing with the review: no public AtomicFsCapabilities ADT. Which consumers actually need which guarantee has not been enumerated yet, and exposing a capability type before that is another premature abstraction. The three guarantees are now named, which is what a future ADT would have to be built from.

Verification: full suite 408, 0 failed, on 3.3.8. scalafmt clean.
